items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I called Joe Muranyi. And we're talking about $500 a week. I couldn't budge him.

ctx.x: Yeah, I know, New York is still Scuffle City.

And the other fat job, Eddie Condon's, pays $35 a night. Now, that's what he just told us, and he lives there. I mean, this is the big deal of being -- and yet, if you're called a New Yorker, -- and I've had that, to call this clarinet player, Joe Muranyi, to go on the road when Volly DeFaut got sick on the tour, and couldn't make it in Greenwich, Connecticut, I called Joe Muranyi. And we're talking about $500 a week. I couldn't budge him. Got that New York address, you know.
Early '40s for me was quite a financial struggle. If you got lucky enough to get a job for $35 a week, you could do a lot of things with that $35. We furnished our apartment and --
